description: Somos un equipo de ingenieros mecatrónicos y estadística. Nos especializamos en sistemas embebidos y análisis de datos avanzado. Vamos a resolver el reto de monitoreo de salud para astronautas creando un prototipo funcional de biofeedback. Buscamos perfiles de Telecomunicaciones y Salud/Medicina ¡Únete a nosotros para construir un proyecto ganador!
summary: POLIS SENSE SPACE is a health-monitoring web app that helps astronauts on long-duration missions detect health changes and act on them, since on those missions crews carry much of that responsibility themselves. Our prototype works without hardware, using manually entered and simulated data. Each of the five crew members has a profile with their health data and a realistic, rotatable 3D body model. The model marks pain areas, colored by pain type, and names the condition when you hover over a zone. Every alert explains why it fired, the possible causes, and step-by-step recommendations, plus a checklist of what is needed to apply them. The app also includes a voice assistant inspired by Baymax. It answers medical questions with reliable feedback, taking into account that the crew is in space, the mission day, and emergencies, and it anticipates pain and gives early estimates like a “fast doctor.” The project uses the NASA data kit to derive health KPIs. It is free and runs on any device through GitHub Pages, with the AI chat served through a Cloudflare Worker using Groq’s free tier. It matters because it helps crews spot problems early and respond when Earth is far away.
details:
Code: The project code (web app, interface, and the Cloudflare Worker that connects the app to the AI model) was developed with the help of Claude (Anthropic), an SI coding assistant. The team directed the work, reviewed the changes through pull requests on GitHub, and tested the result. Code files and the repository acknowledge this assistance in descriptive text and commit metadata.

Runtime AI feature: The in-app voice/chat assistant is powered by a large language model served through Groq (free tier), reached via a Cloudflare Worker. Its answers are generated by SI at the moment of use and are not pre-written. They are not medical advice, and the app is a prototype, not a medical device.
